title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 775-776): X is a real surface (the Longue Marche setting of topological surfaces, here assumed differentiable at a point x). D_x^* denotes the punctured germ of disc at x. The category Germesrevdiff(X,x) has as objects germs of differentiable arcs gamma ending at x. A morphism gamma -> gamma' is an isomorphism between the universal coverings of D_x^* 'pointed' by gamma and gamma'. These are the coverings D^{*~}_{x,gamma}: the arc lifts to the universal cover, so an arc acts as a base point at x. S_x is the circle of half-lines in Tang_x(X), i.e. the boundary circle of the real oriented blow-up of X at x.

The goal (79) is an equivalence Germesrevdiff(X,x) -> Pi_1(S_x) that sends each arc to its half-tangent. Concretely, (80) asks for a canonical bijection Isom(gamma,gamma') = Isom(D^{*~}_{x,gamma}, D^{*~}_{x,gamma'}) -> {homotopy classes of paths in S_x from Delta to Delta'}, where Delta and Delta' are the half-tangents.

On this page Grothendieck switches strategy. Rather than build (80) directly, he builds a functor (81) Theta: Pi_1(S_x) -> Revetements(D_x^*), which is to be an equivalence onto the category of (universal) coverings of D_x^*. To produce functors out of Pi_1(S_x) he gives a combinatorial presentation.
- (82): A_x is the set of closed, 1-connected, proper subsets of S_x. These are the closed arcs of the circle, together with the points (see the transcription correction), but not S_x itself.
- A_x, ordered by inclusion, is viewed as a category. Its enveloping groupoid Gr(A_x) (formally invert all arrows) is canonically equivalent to Pi_1(S_x).
- Page 776 makes this precise. Restrict to the full subcategory Gr_0 on the singleton objects. An arc A with endpoints a and b gives inclusions a -> A <- b, hence an arrow a -> b, which is sent to the class of A traversed as a path from a to b.
- Hence a functor Pi_1(S_x) -> G into any groupoid is the same as a functor A_x -> G, i.e. data indexed by arcs, compatible with inclusions.

The intended use: each arc of directions corresponds to a sector of D_x^*, which is contractible. Hence the universal covering trivializes over it, and one gets functorial data indexed by sectors. This is the classical sector / real-blow-up description of tangential base points.
errors: Minor internal inconsistency or ambiguity: (82) as machine-transcribed excludes points, yet p.776 uses the singleton objects of Gr(A_x). Reading the image, the text most likely says arcs 'ou réduits à des pts' (points included), so there is no actual error.

The claim Gr(A_x) ~ Pi_1(S_x) is correct but unproved here; it is called 'on sait'. It follows from the nerve of the poset of closed proper arcs being homotopy equivalent to S^1 (McCord/Quillen-type argument), and from the fundamental groupoid of a category being its localization at all arrows.
Only the requirement 'differentiable at x' is stated. One needs X to be a C^1 surface near x so that half-tangents and sectors behave well.

ideas.what: Germs of arcs ending at a puncture used as base points for the fundamental groupoid of the punctured disc, with morphisms identified with paths in the circle of directions
ideas.modern_name: tangential base points / real oriented blow-up (Kato–Nakayama-type boundary circle)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (1989, Le groupe fondamental de la droite projective moins trois points); Ihara; folklore in topology
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme alludes to suitable base points for fundamental groupoids of curves; whether La Longue Marche itself develops tangential base points is unsure

ideas.what: Equivalence Pi_1(S_x) ~ category of universal coverings of the punctured disc (Theta)
ideas.modern_name: homotopy equivalence of the punctured disc with the boundary circle of the oriented blow-up

ideas.what: Fundamental groupoid of S^1 presented as the enveloping groupoid (localization) of the poset of closed proper arcs; functors out of Pi_1 given by data on arcs
ideas.modern_name: fundamental groupoid of a poset/category via localization; nerve theorem / McCord; Quillen
ideas.where_published: Ideas of this kind (categories/posets as models of homotopy types) pervade Pursuing Stacks (1983)

missed.claim: A careful, sector-based construction of what are now called tangential base points, in the topological-surface setting of the Longue Marche (c. 1981). This would be roughly contemporaneous with or before Deligne's 1989 formalization. It is of modest historical interest for priority, not new mathematics.
missed.quote: Je vais définir une équivalence de catégories Germesrevdiff(X,x) -> Pi_1(S_x) ... sa demi-tangente
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Documents Grothendieck's own handling of base points at punctures, which is central to Grothendieck–Teichmüller and anabelian work. The mathematics itself is standard.

deep.surprise_reason: Careful but standard topology: the oriented blow-up circle as a model for punctured-disc base points, and the localization of the poset of arcs as Pi_1(S^1). The only point of interest is historical, as an early explicit tangential-base-point construction in Grothendieck's hand.
transcription_corrections: (82): '[-...-] non[?] réduits à des pts' should most likely read '... ou réduits à des pts' (points allowed), consistent with p.776 using singleton objects.
(80) right side: 'classes de chemins dans S_x de Delta à Delta'' — the star on S^*_x is probably a slip or ornament; the paths are in S_x (Isom_{Pi_1 S_x}).
Previous page 'Germesrevdiff' / 'germe d'revt[?]' is likely 'germes d'arcs (différentiables)', given 'si gamma, gamma' sont deux tels arcs'.
